items.headline: US tariffs spare Sri Lanka
items.summary: Washington announced new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China (up to 40%), Vietnam, India, Japan and the EU (20–25% for most). Sri Lanka was left off the list.

items.headline: Reservoir spill gates opened as rain persists
items.summary: Six Deduru Oya spill gates were opened, releasing about 4,200 cubic feet per second. Two Thabbowa Reservoir gates were due to open by 10 PM, and people living downstream along both rivers have been told to stay alert.

items.headline: Teachers' sick-leave action goes ahead Nov 30
items.summary: The Teachers and Principals Trade Union Alliance will hold its sick-leave campaign on 30 November as planned. It says talks with the Prime Minister brought no favourable response to its demands.

items.headline: NCPA logs 9,600 child complaints in nine months
items.summary: The National Child Protection Authority recorded 9,613 complaints from January to September, including 169 child rape cases and 51 teenage pregnancies. Colombo, Gampaha and Kurunegala had the most cases, and a doctors' union is calling for a national child protection policy.

items.headline: President: use allocated funds or lose them
items.summary: President Dissanayake told ministries to plan projects at the start of the year and review them monthly. Unspent funds will go back to the Treasury unless conditions such as opened letters of credit are met. The meeting also discussed a land bank to speed up land allocation for investors.

items.headline: PM pledges action over Kinniya auditorium
items.summary: Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya told Parliament that legal action will follow if wrongdoing is confirmed in the 2022 demolition of a school auditorium in Kinniya. She promised to table all related documents.

items.headline: Fisheries talks set for 22 January
items.summary: Newsfirst reports that the India–Sri Lanka talks on the fisheries dispute will be held in New Delhi on 22 January. Both sides are aiming for a lasting solution.

items.headline: CSE rebounds; ASPI back above 21,300
items.summary: The ASPI rose 0.35% to close at 21,315.84 on turnover of about Rs. 1.45 billion, with banks the most active sector. Foreign investors were net sellers.

items.headline: CMC to settle Rs. 1.04 bn VAT arrears
items.summary: The Colombo Municipal Council told a magistrate it will quickly settle VAT it has owed since 2016. The court asked both sides to report the settlement details on 24 March.

items.headline: Bomb scare at Mattala airport
items.summary: An Azur Air flight from Moscow was searched at Mattala after a bomb scare. A flight from Uzbekistan was reportedly diverted to Katunayake.

items.headline: Suspect remanded over defamatory Facebook posts
items.summary: A Nugegoda man accused of posting manipulated audio and images to defame a Jayaratne Group director was refused bail. He is remanded until 3 December.

items.headline: Eisenkot gains first coalition partner
items.summary: Israel's Gadi Eisenkot secured his first coalition partner as he tries to form a government.

items.headline: Solomon Islands signs Australia security pact
items.summary: The Solomon Islands signed a security agreement with Australia.
